data.name: Fiacre
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'ficus' meaning fig tree and 'ater' meaning water, Fiacre is a name rooted in ancient spiritual traditions. In Christian legend, Fiacre was a hermit known for his faithfulness and miraculous healings. This name is a powerful reminder of the enduring power of faith and the healing properties of nature.

in_hebrew.name: פיאקר
in_hebrew.meaning: פיאקר משמעות שם נוצרי הקדוש פיאקר מאירלנד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פיאקר הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם של הקדוש פיאקר, מיסיונר אירי שחי במאה ה-7. השם פיאקר נגזר מהמילה הגאלית 'fiach', שפירושה 'עורב', ו-'adhar', שפירושה 'גבר'. הקדוש פיאקר היה ידוע בקדושתו ובפעילותו המיסיונרית באירלנד ובצרפת, והוא נחשב לאחד מהקדושים החשובים ביותר של הכנסייה הקתולית באירלנד.

in_greek.name: Φιάκρη
in_greek.meaning: Φιάκρη όνομα χριστιανός του Αγίου Φιάκρη Ιρλανδίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Φιάκρη είναι χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από τον Άγιο Φιάκρη, Ιρλανδό ιεραπόστολο που έζησε τον 7ο αιώνα. Το όνομα Φιάκρη προέρχεται από την γαελική λέξη 'fiach', που σημαίνει 'κόρακας', και 'adhar', που σημαίνει 'άνδρας'. Ο Άγιος Φιάκρη ήταν γνωστός για την αγιότητά του και την ιεραποστολική του δραστηριότητα στην Ιρλανδία και τη Γαλλία, και θεωρείται ένας από τους πιο σημαντικούς αγίους της Καθολικής Εκκλησίας στην Ιρλανδία.

in_latin.name: Fiacre
in_latin.meaning: Fiacre nomen christianum Sancti Fiacri Hiberniae
in_latin.long_meaning: Fiacre est nomen christianum quod originem trahit a Sancto Fiacri, missionario Hiberniae qui saeculo VII floruit. Nomen Fiacre derivatum est a voce gallica 'fiach', quae 'corvum' significat, et 'adhar', quod 'virum' significat. Sanctus Fiacre notus fuit propter sanctitatem et activitatem missionariam in Hibernia et Gallia, et habetur pro uno ex sanctis maximis Ecclesiae Catholicae in Hibernia.

in_english.name: Fiacre
in_english.meaning: Fiacre is a Christian name of Irish origin meaning 'raven' or 'dark-haired'
in_english.long_meaning: Fiacre is a Christian name with Irish roots, derived from the Gaelic words 'fiach', meaning 'raven' or 'dark-haired', and 'adhar', meaning 'man'. The name Fiacre is associated with Saint Fiacre, an Irish missionary who lived in the 7th century and was known for his piety and missionary work in Ireland and France. As a given name, Fiacre symbolizes strength, spirituality, and devotion. It is often chosen for its unique and historic significance in Christian tradition.

saint_reference.note: Saint Fiacre was an Irish monk and hermit who lived in the 7th century. He is revered as a saint in the Catholic Church and is often invoked for his protection and blessings.

data.cultural_impact: The name Fiacre is deeply embedded in the Catholic tradition and is celebrated as the patron saint of gardeners and travelers. Legend has it that St. Fiacre was a monk who lived in France during the seventh century. He was known for his deep devotion to God and for his healing abilities. He was so devoted to his faith that he preferred to spend his days in solitude, living as a hermit in a small cell among the trees. Despite his devotion, Fiacre's fame spread far and wide, and people came from all over to be healed by his touch.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Fiacre is a powerful reminder of the spiritual connection between faith, healing, and nature. The Latin words 'ficus' meaning fig tree and 'ater' meaning water, underscore the significance of this name in the spiritual tradition. The fig tree is a symbol of faith and wisdom, while water is a symbol of life and renewal. Fiacre's name is a powerful reminder of the enduring power of faith and the healing properties of nature. Through his life and miraculous healings, Fiacre embodied the idea that faith can move mountains and heal even the most grievous wounds. The name Fiacre inspires us to have faith in the healing power of God and to remember that nature is a powerful and renewing force in our lives.
